get returns the value without moving the node to the most recent end
put does not check capacity
The map stores values instead of nodes
Eviction removes from the most recent end
fields.Correct: get returns the value without moving the node to the most recent end
fields.Explanation: A read is a use, so get must refresh recency. A missing capacity check would fail put tests too. Storing values breaks moves for every operation, not only after get. Wrong end eviction fails without get.

fields.Question: In Python, which standard library type gives an LRU cache with move_to_end and popitem(last=False)?
fields.Choices:
collections.OrderedDict
dict
collections.deque
heapq
fields.Correct: collections.OrderedDict
fields.Explanation: OrderedDict supports O(1) move_to_end and popping from either end. A plain dict keeps insertion order but has no move_to_end. A deque cannot remove an arbitrary key in O(1). heapq has no key lookup.

fields.Question: Time Based Key-Value Store: set(key, value, t) with strictly increasing t per key, get(key, t) returns the value with the largest timestamp <= t. Best get?
fields.Choices:
Binary search the per key list of (t, value) with bisect_right on t
Linear scan from the end
Store a dict of every timestamp
Sort the list on every get
fields.Correct: Binary search the per key list of (t, value) with bisect_right on t
fields.Explanation: Appends keep each list sorted, so bisect_right on the timestamps (a parallel list or key=) finds the floor in O(log n). Scanning is O(n). A per timestamp dict cannot find the floor of a missing t. Sorting on each get is O(n log n).

fields.Question: Sliding window rate limiter: at most N requests per user in the last W seconds, exact. Which per user structure?
fields.Choices:
A single last request timestamp
A min heap of all timestamps across users
A deque of timestamps, pop from the left while older than now - W
A counter reset every W seconds
fields.Correct: A deque of timestamps, pop from the left while older than now - W
fields.Explanation: The deque holds exactly the requests in the window and each timestamp is popped once. A fixed window counter allows up to 2N across a boundary. One timestamp cannot count requests. A global heap mixes users and costs log n.

fields.Question: Insert Delete GetRandom in O(1) average. How does remove work?
fields.Choices:
Use a set and random.choice(list(set))
Swap the item with the last element in the array, update its index in the map, then pop
Remove from the array with list.remove
Mark it deleted and skip it in getRandom
fields.Correct: Swap the item with the last element in the array, update its index in the map, then pop
fields.Explanation: Swapping with the last keeps the array dense so pop is O(1) and random indexing stays uniform. list.remove is O(n). Tombstones make getRandom non uniform or unbounded. Converting a set to a list is O(n).
fields.Hint: Fill the hole with the last.

fields.Question: LFU Cache with O(1) operations, ties broken by least recently used. What extra state beyond key to node?
fields.Choices:
Frequency to ordered list of keys, plus the current minimum frequency
A min heap of (frequency, time)
Only a counter per key
A sorted list of frequencies
fields.Correct: Frequency to ordered list of keys, plus the current minimum frequency
fields.Explanation: Buckets per frequency with recency order, plus min frequency, give O(1) eviction. A heap is O(log n). Counters alone cannot find the victim quickly. A sorted list is O(n) to update.

fields.Question: Flatten Nested List Iterator. Lazy approach that keeps hasNext correct with empty nested lists like [[], [[]]]?
fields.Choices:
Flatten everything in the constructor and ignore laziness
next pops a list and returns its first item
hasNext returns True if the stack is non empty
A stack of iterators; hasNext advances until it finds an integer
fields.Correct: A stack of iterators; hasNext advances until it finds an integer
fields.Explanation: hasNext must skip empty lists, so it does the advancing. Eager flattening works but is not lazy, which the question asks for. Returning a list's first item fails on nested lists. A non empty stack can hold only empty lists, so True is wrong.

fields.Question: Design an in memory key value store with begin, set, get, rollback and commit, where transactions can nest. What structure?
fields.Answer: A base dict plus a stack of change layers. set writes to the top layer. get checks layers from top to bottom, then the base, and needs a tombstone for deletes. rollback pops the top layer. commit merges the top layer into the one below (or the base). Each operation is O(depth) for get, O(1) for set.
fields.Source: Anthropic software engineer interview guide, IGotAnOffer (https://igotanoffer.com/en/advice/anthropic-software-engineer-interview)

fields.Question: Design a spreadsheet where cells hold numbers or formulas referencing other cells. How do you update dependents and detect cycles?
fields.Answer: Keep a dependency graph from a cell to cells that use it. On set, parse references, check for a cycle with DFS from the new references back to the cell, then recompute dependents in topological order. Cache values and invalidate only reachable dependents.
